title: warpScalar
body:
## warpScalar

Displaces each point along a direction by scale times a point scalar (new position = point + scale x value x direction), turning a field on a flat surface into a relief or carpet plot, or moving a surface by a normal displacement. With useNormal true (Schemaxis default) every point moves along the same normal (default z+); with useNormal false the input's point normals are used when present. The output keeps the input type, except that image data and rectilinear grids become a structured grid; all arrays are carried along.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- The warp distance is in dataset units: choose scale so that the field range times scale is a modest fraction of the geometry size, otherwise the relief dwarfs or hides the shape.
- Schemaxis normalizes normal, so its length does not change the displacement; express any magnification through scale.
- Schemaxis's serial native acceptance run (examples/schemaxis/extended-coverage.json) executes this operation once, on a planar slice with a linear field; it does not check this operation's output values, so inspect the result on your own data.

Native constructor: `WarpByScalar`. Identity: `curated binding`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

| Port | Meaning / native port | Required | Multiplicity | Kind | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | Required data input for the native Input port. Give the name of the upstream node to connect, or a {node, port} object to use another of its output ports. Accepted data: explicit-point datasets (polygonal, unstructured or structured grids) (vtkPointSet); image data (uniform rectilinear grids) (vtkImageData); rectilinear grids (vtkRectilinearGrid). | True | one object | `data` | `{"compatibility":"native-domain-checked","composite":null,"cost":{"basis":"no benchmark","conversion":"none inserted","rating":"unknown"},"nativeTypes":["vtkPointSet","vtkImageData","vtkRectilinearGrid"],"requirements":{},"traits":{"contiguity":"unknown","indexing":"unknown","iteration":"unknown"}}` |

### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `field` | Two entries naming the scalar that sets the displacement: the association token POINTS and the array name, e.g. ["POINTS", "height"]. Each point moves by scale times its value along the warp direction, so negative values move points the opposite way. | `{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string","minLength":1},"minItems":2,"maxItems":2}` | `required` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE","REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `scale` | The scalar value at a given point is multiplied by the value of this property to determine the magnitude of the change vector for that point. | `{"type":"number"}` | `1` | `1` |
| `normal` | Direction along which points are displaced, as an axis token, a vector or an azimuth/elevation object; Schemaxis normalizes it to unit length. It applies to every point while useNormal is true, and when useNormal is false only if the input has no point normals. | `{"type":"union","title":"direction","summary":"An axis token, a vector, or an azimuth and elevation about an up axis","options":[{"type":"string","title":"axis token such as 'x+' or 'z-'"},{"type":"array","title":"vector [x, y, z]","items":{"type":"number"},"minItems":3,"maxItems":3},{"type":"object","title":"direction object","properties":{"axis":{"type":"string","summary":"Axis token such as 'x+'"},"azimuth":{"type":"number","minimum":-360,"maximum":360,"summary":"Degrees about the up axis from the reference axis"},"elevation":{"type":"number","minimum":-180,"maximum":180,"summary":"Degrees tilted from the plane perpendicular to up"},"vector":{"type":"array","title":"vector [x, y, z]","items":{"type":"number"},"minItems":3,"maxItems":3},"up":{"type":"union","title":"up direction","options":[{"type":"string","title":"axis token such as 'z+'"},{"type":"array","title":"vector [x, y, z]","items":{"type":"number"},"minItems":3,"maxItems":3}]}}}]}` | `[0,0,1]` | `[0,0,1]` |
| `useNormal` | When true, every point moves along normal and any point normals in the input are ignored. Set it to false to displace a curved surface along its own point normals, e.g. a normal-displacement field on a hull; normal is then used only if the input has no point normals. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `true` | `true` |

Cross-option checks:

```json
[
  {
    "kind": "firstItem",
    "option": "field",
    "values": [
      "POINTS"
    ],
    "code": "INVALID_ASSOCIATION",
    "message": "warpScalar reads the selected array per point; the CELLS association is not supported",
    "recovery": "name a POINTS array; convert cell data first with cellToPoint"
  }
]
```

Execution contract:

```json
{
  "mode": "serial",
  "performance": "unknown"
}
```

### Syntax example

Place in `nodes`. Data outputs may be selected by a scene; resource outputs must be connected to a compatible consumer.

```json
{
  "id": "result",
  "filter": "warpScalar",
  "inputs": {
    "input": "UPSTREAM_input"
  },
  "options": {
    "field": [
      "REPLACE_WITH_VALUE",
      "REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"
    ]
  }
}
```
